card.title: Exam bank — every board question on DC circuits

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Two questions carry this unit: Kirchhoff's laws applied to a circuit (5 marks: KCL = charge conservation at junctions, KVL = energy conservation around loops, worked on two cells + resistor giving 0.71 A) and the parallel-resistor numerical (2/3/6 ohm on 12 V gives 1 ohm, 12 A). Drift velocity and internal resistance trail behind.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: KCL: sum-I = 0 · KVL: sum-EMF = sum-IR · parallel 1/R = sum-1/Ri · series R = sum-Ri · V = E - Ir · divider V1 = V*R1/(R1+R2)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: KCL needs lumped junctions (no charge pile-up); KVL needs no changing magnetic flux through the loop (why it holds for DC networks). Parallel reciprocal-addition assumes the same voltage across all branches — the meaning of 'parallel'. Internal-resistance sag V = E - Ir assumes the simple E+r source model.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: 2/3/6 ohm parallel: reciprocals 3/6+2/6+1/6 = 1, so R = 1 ohm exactly (currents split 6/4/2 A, inverse to resistance). Two cells E1 = 2 V, E2 = 3 V with R = 5 ohm, r = 1 ohm each: total E = 5 V, total R = 7 ohm, I = 0.71 A. Short circuit: load to zero, current capped only by r.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: NEB 2021 (4): 1/R = 1/2+1/3+1/6 = 1, so R = 1 ohm; I = V/R = 12/1 = 12 A drawn. NEB 2022 (5): state KCL (junction currents sum to zero — charge conserved) + KVL (loop EMFs equal drops — energy conserved), then solve the two-cell circuit for 0.71 A with sign discipline around the loop.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Mark-losers: adding parallel resistors directly; sign errors traversing loops against current; forgetting internal r in 'real battery' questions. Kirchhoff's loop law fails with induced EMF — DC-only territory.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: No heavy derivation is asked — the 'derivation' IS Kirchhoff applied: label all branch currents, write one junction equation, write loop equations (rise = drop with signs), solve simultaneously. Drift-velocity relation I = nAev_d derives Ohm microscopically (rho = m/ne2tau) as backup theory.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: 'State Kirchhoff' means junction (charge) + loop (energy) + one solved circuit. Two-resistor parallel: product/sum. Equal R in parallel: R/n. Always redraw the circuit with currents labelled before writing equations.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB 2022 (5): Kirchhoff's laws + solved circuit current. NEB 2021 (4): 2/3/6 ohm parallel on 12 V — total R and current. That is the complete bank.
